open_points.subject: consumer snapshots versus the single home of personal data
open_points.text: “Every other service ... reads that identity as a snapshot” and “the snapshot a consumer keeps” conflict with “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it issued” and “Other services keep no customer record and no copy of these values.”
open_points.question: May PresuPro, Cabinet or Client Portal persist any fields returned by `context`, `read a project` or `list projects`; if so, which fields and for what purpose?
options: No service may persist them; reads are transient
Services may persist complete authorized snapshots
Only Client Portal may persist its expressly allowed offline publication
Each service may persist a specified projection
open_points.default_guess: Treat Registry reads by PresuPro and Cabinet as transient and permit only Client Portal's expressly allowed offline projection and issued documents to persist values.

open_points.subject: start of the single-home guarantee
open_points.text: “Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data” is stated as current fact, while R0-80 says “Removing the stores and copies the services keep today is each service's own change.”
open_points.question: When does the single-home promise become effective, and may production Registry launch while another service still keeps a living customer record or copied values?
options: The guarantee is a launch precondition
The guarantee begins only after all service migrations finish
Temporary duplicate stores are allowed during a declared transition
Registry does not verify or gate this external condition
open_points.default_guess: Make removal of the other services' living copies a production-readiness precondition, verified outside Registry.

open_points.subject: fiscal-data ownership
open_points.text: R0-37 says “fiscal data stays in PresuPro,” while R0-80 says fiscal data “are held only by Registry” and “PresuPro keeps none” outside issued documents.
open_points.question: Is the R0-37 customer bullet superseded so that Registry is the sole living store of tax id and legal name?
options: Registry is the sole living store
PresuPro remains the living store
Both temporarily store fiscal data during migration
open_points.default_guess: Treat the R0-37 sentence as superseded and make Registry the sole living store.

open_points.subject: billing-data customer name
open_points.text: R0-06 defines “Name, phone, e-mail and language” as contact data and R0-80 says “contact data still reaches the owner alone,” but `read a customer's billing data` returns “name, kind, tax id, legal name” to PresuPro.
open_points.question: May PresuPro receive the Customer's ordinary `name`, or only the fiscal/legal name and non-contact billing fields?
options: Return ordinary name and legal name to PresuPro
Return only kind, tax id and legal name
Redefine ordinary name as billing data rather than contact data
Use legal name when present and otherwise refuse document issuance
open_points.default_guess: Return only kind, tax id and legal name; keep the ordinary contact name owner-only.

open_points.subject: customer erasure after fiscal data was added
open_points.text: The action is “erase a customer's contact data” and says “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone,” but also says the Customer “keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased” after tax id and legal name were added to the record.
open_points.question: Does this erasure also remove kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-ended state, or does it retain some of them?
options: Erase every field except `customer_ref` and the erased marker
Erase contact fields but retain fiscal and lifecycle fields
Provide separate contact-data and whole-record anonymisation actions
open_points.default_guess: Erase every field except the identity and erased marker, following the explicit “keeps only” promise.

open_points.subject: agent projection free-text values
open_points.text: The action promises “no ... other personal value,” and the Agent actor says the projection is “without personal values,” while R0-68 says room names and artifact pointer values are not inspected and a value that breaks the writer rule “does reach the agent.”
open_points.question: Is the guarantee merely that fields classified by Registry as `personal_data` are excluded, or must Registry prevent personal values embedded in room names and pointer fields from reaching the agent?
options: Guarantee only exclusion of fields classified as `personal_data`
Validate or redact room names and pointer values
Remove free-text room and pointer fields from the agent projection
Accept the leakage risk but state it as a failure of the guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Limit the guarantee to Registry-classified `personal_data` fields and explicitly describe room names and pointer values as uninspected writer-controlled data.

open_points.subject: anonymised project retained identifiers and pointers
open_points.text: R0-71 says an anonymised project “holds no personal value,” but it retains its project id and artifact pointers; R0-26 says a project id “is not anonymous by itself,” and R0-68 says pointer fields can contain personal values that Registry does not inspect.
open_points.question: What must be true of the retained project id and pointer fields before Registry may call the project anonymised?
options: The owner/governance attests that retained values cannot re-identify anyone
Registry removes or redacts identifying pointer fields
Registry deletes the project whenever retained values may identify someone
`anonymised` is only a structural state and carries no no-personal-data guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Require an external governance attestation before the owner chooses anonymisation; otherwise require whole deletion.

open_points.subject: significant audit changes
open_points.text: R0-58 records “only significant changes of state,” lists some examples, and also says “Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded.” It does not classify room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, pending access requests, answered requests, relationship ending/resuming, or the one-time import.
open_points.question: Exactly which primary actions create audit entries, especially state-changing actions performed through Kernel?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action
Audit only the categories explicitly enumerated in R0-58
Audit project/customer/access changes but not artifacts or pending requests
Declare an explicit per-action audit flag
open_points.default_guess: Declare an explicit per-action rule and audit every accepted state-changing primary action except where State 0 expressly excludes it.

open_points.subject: customer and project revision checks on non-correction actions
open_points.text: R0-35 says “A change states the revision it was made against” and every accepted project or customer change moves its revision, but stale-revision failure is stated only for `correct a project` and `correct a customer`, not archive, customer erasure, restriction changes, or relationship end/resume.
open_points.question: Must every mutation of a Project or Customer supply its expected revision, return the next revision, and refuse a stale revision?
options: Yes, every Project and Customer mutation
Only correction actions use optimistic concurrency
Only owner-interface edits use revisions; command-like transitions do not
open_points.default_guess: Require the expected revision and stale refusal for every Project or Customer mutation, including archive and all customer lifecycle actions.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: `read the session's access` returns “the access version,” but no text says which actions increment it, whether owner changes must state an expected version, or whether replacing a pending request changes it.
open_points.question: What does the access version version, when does it advance, and does it provide stale-change protection for grants, revocations, active-project changes and request answers?
options: It versions every change to grants, active project and pending request
It versions only grants and active-project changes
It is informational and supplies no concurrency check
Remove it until a versioned access contract is defined
open_points.default_guess: Version the complete access record and require the owner to submit the expected version for every mutation of that record.

open_points.subject: answering a request when the selected project cannot be granted
open_points.text: `answer an access request` says granting adds “the project the owner picks from the catalogue” and lists only “a request no longer pending” as failure, while granting an unknown or archived project is refused elsewhere.
open_points.question: If the selected project is archived, erased, deleted, or otherwise ceases to be grantable before the answer is applied, is the answer refused, and does the pending request remain?
options: Refuse atomically and leave the request pending
Refuse and clear the request
Treat it as a decline and clear the request
Grant archived projects but do not make them active
open_points.default_guess: Refuse atomically and leave the pending request unchanged.

open_points.subject: migration project selection
open_points.text: R0-79 says “The owner picks the projects: today” followed by two named projects, while the action accepts “the projects the owner picks” and permanently closes import after the first success.
open_points.question: Is the import restricted to exactly the two named project ids, may the owner choose either subset, or may the owner select any projects present in the VPS export?
options: Exactly the two named projects
Any subset of the two named projects
Any projects in the VPS export
A separately approved fixed allowlist
open_points.default_guess: Restrict the migration to the two named ids and let the owner choose either or both in the single import.

open_points.subject: repeated customer lifecycle transitions
open_points.text: The actions “restrict or lift a restriction” and “end or resume a customer relationship” do not say what happens when the requested state already holds.
open_points.question: Are repeated restrict, lift, end and resume commands idempotent, refused, or accepted as new changes with new revisions, dates and audit entries?
options: Return the unchanged Customer without moving revision
Refuse an already-satisfied transition
Accept it as a new change and move revision
Use different rules for dated end and boolean restriction
open_points.default_guess: Return the unchanged Customer without moving its revision or adding a state-change audit entry.
